correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the two-torus Fourier decomposition with selected modes (-Nq,q) and the modewise Bessel triple-product Mellin representation. The primary Bessel bound gives I1(s)>0; explicit |J_n| majorants and R_q>= (29/50)Nq bound the q>=2 tail by a q^2-weighted geometric sum. Checked the derived gamma ratio R(k,alpha), its logarithmic monotonicity in s, the base exact-rational estimate R(23,0)<0.8, and the uniform ratio bound <0.95 (finite exact checker addresses base/exponential Taylor inequalities; analytic inequalities prove all k). The derivative tail is smaller than epsilon_k times the positive first sine via |sin(q phi)|<=q sin phi, yielding strict monotonicity and uniform cosine remainder. At even endpoint powers there is no phase response; they are correctly excluded. No finite k enumeration is misused as an infinite proof.

The independent full-text source inspection confirms the relevant distinction; older majorant and finite-cyclic/even-moment results do not supply the continuum phase theorem.

value.rationale: Optimizing over the unimodular coefficient circle is a natural stronger variant of the original majorant problem. It identifies every phase, unique extrema and quantitative closeness to a cosine in a nontrivial infinite degree/exponent regime; the cutoff k>=23 is explicitly merely sufficient.

limitations: No claim about smaller degrees, any different third frequency, or coefficients with variable magnitudes.
No uniform nonzero first-mode amplitude at p endpoints.
